note: Discriminating probes. Each record exists because two defensible readings of SPEC.md produce DIFFERENT derive() output on it, and ideally on nothing else.

probes.ambiguity: §5.1 'class precedence is absolute ... even when the witness is a descendant' vs §5.2 'descendant wins' within a class. Does an override that is an ANCESTOR beat a task that is its DESCENDANT?
Same question, the other direction: a witness that DESCENDS from the task. The spec's parenthetical suggests task wins; a naive reading of 'descendant wins' gives the witness.
§5.2 tie-break order is stated as 'most intent ancestors, fewest witness ancestors, smallest id'. Are these applied in that ORDER (lexicographic) or weighted?
probes.split: smallest-id -> x=a ; reverse order would also give a here, so this probe needs a wider net

probes.ambiguity: Two same-class candidates where the 'most intent ancestors' criterion and the 'fewest witness ancestors' criterion point at DIFFERENT records.
probes.split: most-intent -> cand2 (descends an override) ; fewest-witness -> cand1

probes.ambiguity: §5.3 'If 2+ DISTINCT values exist'. Do two records agreeing on a value produce a conflict entry anyway?
§5.4 Kahn 'smallest-id-first'. Do cycle-affected records appear in `order` at all, or are they dropped?
§5.5 'the orphan's descendants are NOT auto-orphaned'. Does the descendant's OWN effects then apply, or is it excluded because its ancestor is missing?
probes.split: kid-applies -> y present ; whole-branch-excluded -> y absent

probes.ambiguity: §2 canonical form sorts object keys by code point. Are `true` and `1` distinct KEYS or does a port coerce?
Does §2's key sorting apply RECURSIVELY into nested objects, or only at the top level of a record?
§1 says ids must be free of \n and :. Is that enforced (reject) or merely documented? The corpus cannot tell, but a port that rejects and a port that accepts will diverge on a hostile input.
Two unrelated same-class records contest a key. Neither is an ancestor of the other, so ancestry cannot decide. Does the spec say which wins?
probes.split: streaming/topo-first -> x=1 ; gather-then-filter as written in 5.2 -> SILENT (both survivors are 'task')

probes.ambiguity: 1.1 says kind defaults to null and other values are 'out of scope for the fold'; 5.1 ranks every record by class. What class does a null-kind record have?
probes.split: null ranks last -> x=from-override ; null throws ; null inherits witness -> x=from-null

probes.ambiguity: 5.1's parenthetical mentions ancestry as an exception. Does that generalise to 'class beats ancestry' everywhere, or is ancestry only a tie-break within a class?
probes.split: class-absolute -> x=1 (witness loses despite descending) ; ancestry-first -> x=2

probes.ambiguity: v0.4.6 says an unclassifiable record 'never displaces a classifiable one' -- silent when NEITHER is classifiable. v0.4.6 follow-up: unclassifiable is a single class, so 5.2 step 3 applies (ancestry, then topo order).
probes.split: single-class + topo-first -> x=1 ; undefined -> no answer

probes.ambiguity: Two unclassifiable records where one descends from the other. Ancestry is consulted 'when the two classes are EQUAL' -- and an unclassifiable record has no class, so the ORIGINAL text never said whether two are equal. Repaired: they are.
kind:'banana' -- is an unrecognised VALUE malformed, or accepted and ranked lowest? 1.1's malformed rule covers a MISSING field. Adjudicated 0.910 for 'accepted, lowest'.
